findings.summary: The caption promises ten pages and coverage of type switches, but the set has eight pages and never mentions type switches or a numbered list of gotchas.
findings.evidence: caption: "Ten pages of field notes: implicit satisfaction, the method-set rule, iface/eface internals, embedding, type switches, and the ten gotchas worth memorising." — the `slides` array contains 8 entries, and no block on any page covers `switch v := i.(type)` or enumerates ten gotchas.
findings.fix: Change to "Eight pages of field notes: implicit satisfaction, the method-set rule, iface/eface internals, embedding, boxing costs, and type assertions." (drop "type switches" and "the ten gotchas"), or add a type-switch page and two more pages to match the claim.

findings.summary: The caption promises ten pages but the carousel has only eight.
findings.evidence: Caption: "Ten pages of field notes: implicit satisfaction, the method-set rule, iface/eface internals, embedding, type switches, and the ten gotchas worth memorising." — the titles array contains 8 entries, ending at "Promotion Rules & Type Assertions".
findings.fix: Change "Ten pages of field notes" to "Eight pages of field notes" (or add the two missing pages so the count matches).

findings.summary: Page 2 shows a decorator `Write` method that delegates through an embedded interface field, but struct embedding and the `cw` type itself are not introduced until pages 7–8.
findings.evidence: Page 2: "func (c *cw) Write(b []byte) (int, error) { c.n += len(b); return c.Writer.Write(b) // delegate }" — the type is only declared on page 8: "type cw struct { io.Writer; n int }".
findings.fix: Delete this block from page 2 (the "Shape, Not Name" structural-vs-nominal section it sits under does not need it) and keep the decorator entirely on page 8, where the `cw` declaration and the embedding rules that make `c.Writer.Write` legal have already been taught.

findings.summary: "`*T` satisfies strictly more interfaces than `T`" is false whenever T has no pointer-receiver methods, in which case the two method sets are identical.
findings.evidence: page 3 bullet: "`*T` satisfies strictly more interfaces than `T`" — but for `type Celsius float64` with only `func (c Celsius) String() string`, method sets of `Celsius` and `*Celsius` are both `{String}`.
findings.fix: Change to "`*T` satisfies at least as many interfaces as `T`, and strictly more as soon as any method has a pointer receiver."

findings.summary: The embedding rules omit that pointer-receiver methods of an embedded value type T are promoted to *S, implying they never promote at all.
findings.evidence: page 4 bullets: "Embed `T` in `S`: value methods promote to `S` and `*S`" / "Embed `*T` in `S`: both sets promote to `S` and `*S`"
findings.fix: Restate per the spec: "Embed `T` in `S`: `T`-receiver methods promote to `S` and `*S`; `*T`-receiver methods promote to `*S` only" and "Embed `*T` in `S`: both sets promote to `S` and `*S`."

findings.summary: Page 4 demonstrates a pointer-receiver escape-to-heap under an unrelated heading, one page before the claim it demonstrates and two pages before boxing is explained.
findings.evidence: Page 4, following the "Slices And Maps Fool You" bullets: "go build -gcflags=-m ./..." / "# moved to heap: c  <- escaped into an iface". The claim it supports appears on page 5 — "Pointer copies one word but may push the value to the heap" — and why storing a value in an interface allocates is only explained on page 6 ("Everything else — even an `int` that would fit — is **boxed**, usually on the heap").
findings.fix: Move this `-gcflags=-m` block to page 5, directly beneath the "Pointer copies one word but may push the value to the heap" bullet under "Binding And Cost".

findings.summary: The `BenchmarkIface` code block on page 5 uses types `Shape` and `rect` that are not declared until page 6.
findings.evidence: Page 5: "func BenchmarkIface(b *testing.B) { var s Shape = rect{2, 3}; for range b.N { sink = s.Area() } }" — page 6 then declares them under "Measuring The Call": "type Shape interface { Area() float64 }" / "type rect struct{ w, h float64 }".
findings.fix: Move the `Shape`/`rect` declarations to page 5, immediately above the benchmark (and above the follow-up bullets about the direct-call and generic `Area[T Shape]` variants), leaving page 6's "Measuring The Call" section to hold the comparison results rather than the type definitions.

findings.summary: Page 5 asserts itab caching and dispatch through `tab.fun[i]` with no named antecedent and two pages before the itab's contents are shown.
findings.evidence: Page 5 bullets: "Built once per (interface, concrete type) pair" / "Cached in a global hash table" / "`w.Write(b)` = load `tab.fun[i]`, indirect call with `data`" — the itab layout ("inter", "_type", "hash", "fun[0..n]") is only drawn on page 7 under "Inside The itab".
findings.fix: Either move the page-7 itab diagram forward to sit directly above these three bullets on page 5, or move the three bullets back to page 7 under "Inside The itab"; at minimum give them their own heading ("The itab") so "Built once per…" has a stated subject.

findings.summary: Page is only 37% full.
findings.evidence: fillPct 37
findings.fix: Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: Page 6 renders only two short sections and leaves roughly the bottom two-thirds of the board blank, so it looks broken next to every other page.
findings.evidence: Content on slide-06.png stops at the 'Free Boxes' card (~y=655 of 1456px); the area from y≈690 to the bottom border at y≈1380 is empty board, whereas pages 1-5, 7 and 8 all run content down to y≈1250-1340.
findings.fix: Re-flow page 6 so its blocks fill the board (move content forward from page 7, or merge page 6 into an adjacent page) instead of emitting a page that terminates a third of the way down.

findings.summary: "A named set of method signatures — nothing else" is no longer accurate: since Go 1.18 an interface may also contain type elements (unions and `~T` approximations).
findings.evidence: page 1 bullet: "A named set of method signatures — nothing else", alongside "`any` is an alias for it since Go 1.18" on the same page.
findings.fix: Qualify it, e.g. "A named set of method signatures (since Go 1.18 interfaces may also hold type elements like `~int | ~string`, but those are constraint-only and cannot be used as variable types)".

findings.summary: The stdlib table lists `io.Reader`'s method without its results, contradicting the same page's definition of a signature.
findings.evidence: page 1: "Signature = name + parameter types + result types" and table row ["`io.Reader`", "`Read([]byte)`"] — the real method is `Read(p []byte) (n int, err error)`.
findings.fix: Change the cell to `Read([]byte) (int, error)` so it matches `Error() string` / `String() string` in the adjacent rows.

findings.summary: The counting-writer decorator counts bytes before delegating, so it over-counts on short or failed writes.
findings.evidence: page 2 code: "func (c *cw) Write(b []byte) (int, error) {" / "\tc.n += len(b)" / "\treturn c.Writer.Write(b) // delegate"
findings.fix: Count what was actually written: `n, err := c.Writer.Write(b); c.n += n; return n, err`.

findings.summary: Page 2's sidebox relies on "embedded interfaces" before embedding is introduced on page 7.
findings.evidence: Page 2 sidebox "Legal / Illegal": "Overlapping names from embedded interfaces: OK if identical (Go 1.14+)" — embedding is first defined on page 7: "type ReadWriter interface { Reader // method sets union; Writer }".
findings.fix: Cut that sidebox line from page 2 (keeping the duplicate-method-name and check-at-assignment lines) since page 7 already carries the identical rule: "Overlapping names legal since Go 1.14 if signatures match".

findings.summary: The `http.HandlerFunc` snippet uses undeclared shorthand types `W` and `R`.
findings.evidence: Page 2: "type HF func(w W, r *R)" / "func (f HF) ServeHTTP(w W, r *R) { f(w, r) }" — neither `W` nor `R` is declared or expanded anywhere in the part.
findings.fix: Use the real names in the snippet — `type HF func(http.ResponseWriter, *http.Request)` and `func (f HF) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { f(w, r) }` — or add a `// W = http.ResponseWriter, R = http.Request` line above it.

findings.summary: "Only the declaring package can satisfy a sealed one" is wrong — an outside type that embeds the sealed interface (or a value implementing it) satisfies it.
findings.evidence: page 3 bullets: "Unexported methods seal an interface, e.g. `testing.TB`" / "Only the declaring package can satisfy a sealed one" — yet `type myTB struct { testing.TB }` compiles and satisfies `testing.TB` from any package.
findings.fix: Reword to "No outside package can implement the unexported method — the only escape is embedding the interface (or a value that implements it), which is how `testing.TB` wrappers are built."

findings.summary: The sugar-trap example on page 3 uses `Counter`/`Inc`, which are only declared on page 4, and an interface `Incr` that is never declared anywhere.
findings.evidence: Page 3: "var v Counter" / "v.Inc()          // ok: rewritten (&v).Inc()" / "var i Incr = v   // compile error" — page 4 then introduces the type: "func (c *Counter) Inc()    { c.n++ }".
findings.fix: Add the two declarations the snippet depends on at the top of the page-3 block — `type Counter struct{ n int }` with `func (c *Counter) Inc()`, and `type Incr interface { Inc() }` — or swap the page-3/page-4 receiver sections so `Counter` is defined first.

findings.summary: The dispatch benchmark on page 5 uses `Shape` and `rect`, which are only declared on page 6, so the snippet references undefined types where it appears.
findings.evidence: page 5: "var s Shape = rect{2, 3}" inside `BenchmarkIface`; page 6 ("Measuring The Call") then declares "type Shape interface { Area() float64 }" and "type rect struct{ w, h float64 }".
findings.fix: Move the `Shape`/`rect` declarations and the "Measuring The Call" heading ahead of the benchmark (or move the benchmark and its three follow-up bullets onto page 6, whose title already promises "Measuring Dispatch").

findings.summary: Connector lines in the 'Inside The itab' diagram are drawn straight through the label text of the stacked boxes instead of terminating at their edges.
findings.evidence: In slide-07.png the vertical connector crosses the glyphs of 'interface type' and splits 'type hash' into 'type|hash'; the same line continues through the box interiors down to 'method pointers'.
findings.fix: Route the itab diagram's edges to stop at each box's boundary (or offset them around the box) so no line crosses a label.

findings.summary: Page 7 states the cost of type assertions before type assertions have been introduced on page 8.
findings.evidence: Page 7, "Dispatch Speed": "Assertions compare the stored type pointer or hash — cheap, not free" — the two assertion forms are first shown on page 8: "s := i.(string)     // panics on mismatch".
findings.fix: Move this bullet to page 8, appending it to the assertion-forms bullet list where `i.(string)` has just been shown.

findings.summary: Connector lines in the 'Name Resolution' diagram pass through box labels rather than stopping at the box borders.
findings.evidence: In slide-08.png the arrow from the 'selector s.M' branch runs through the text of 'shadows, wins' and continues across the 'promoted' box toward 'ambiguous: error'.
